modules.name: auth
modules.summary: Who is using the app. The Kernel owns accounts and sessions; the app only reads the current one.
notes: Visibility decides who may open the app shell. It never grants data access on its own.

The Deployment's Signup Policy, which the owner sets in the editor or with signup_policy_set, decides who may create an account: Open, Invitation only, Closed or an Allowlist. Under Invitation only, the sign-in page offers no account creation; invited people accept from the link in their email, which opens /_littlebox/invitation.

modules.name: actions
modules.summary: The only door to the database. A call names a Server Action declared in actions.json and passes its input; the Kernel authorizes the caller, binds the input and runs the action's one SQL statement, or records its Signal.
notes: A query action returns the rows of its SELECT. Column names are exactly the ones the SELECT projects, so alias any expression the app reads.
A mutation action returns { changes, lastInsertId }. Read changed rows with a separate query.

The Action Contract, action-contract.json, lists every action with its inputs, the columns it returns, its errors and limits. It is written from actions.json and schema.sql by littlebox contract and carried in the export; an expression the SELECT returns without AS has no name in it, and the Validation Gate warns.

To record that something happened, such as a signup to a newsletter or a finished lesson, declare a signal on the mutation that does it, or add an action of kind signal and call it with miniapp.actions.call. There is no other tracking call.
A call the Kernel refuses records no Signal and counts in no Usage total.

declarations.summary: { "name": "order.placed", "properties"?: ["input binding keys"] } on a mutation, or on an action of "kind": "signal" that has access and bindings but no statement. When the action succeeds the Kernel records the Signal with the named inputs as its properties, in the Deployment's Usage store. A signal action runs no SQL and returns { recorded: true }. The owner reads Signals with signals_read; the app cannot. The Validation Gate and the Kernel refuse the same declarations with the same messages.
limits: 8 properties per Signal; a string property keeps its first 128 bytes
a signal action counts toward the action limit like any other action
a signal action cannot declare http
the Kernel keeps the newest 50,000 Signals per Deployment and drops the oldest

modules.name: http
modules.summary: Routes on the Deployment's own host for programs and other services: a JSON endpoint, a webhook, a file a program fetches. There is no browser call; the app's own pages keep using miniapp.actions.call, and may use a file's route as an img src.
notes: Only an action declared anonymous may bind a route, and the route answers whatever the Deployment's visibility. On a private app, a route without a signature is open to anyone who knows the path.

A route has three kinds of caller: a service that signs the request, a program that sends Authorization: Bearer with an API key the owner issued, and a person signed in to the app, from the app's own origin. An actor binding yields the key's ID or the user's ID; a signed request has no actor.
A signed route reads the declared header as t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>" keyed with the secret>. An API key that names the action replaces the signature.
The owner sets the secret with the secret_set admin tool before publishing. It never appears in actions.json, the Build Artifact or an export.

GET /_littlebox/files/<id> returns a file the caller may read, with its own type. A person reads by the usual file rules, a visitor reads public files of a public app, and an API key reads the visibilities the owner named on it.
The editor preview serves no routes. Run them on a Development Kernel with littlebox dev, or on a Deployment.

declarations.summary: { "method": "GET" | "POST", "path": "/api/items", "signature"?: { "header": "X-Signature", "secret": "items_webhook" } } on an action declared anonymous. GET binds a query and maps the query string onto its input bindings by type; POST binds a mutation and reads a JSON object body. The route answers { result } with the rows or { changes, lastInsertId }, and { error } with a status code. The Validation Gate and the Kernel refuse the same declarations with the same messages.
limits: a signature's t within 300 seconds of the Kernel's clock, and each signature accepted once
the runtime endpoint's action rate limits: 30 per 10 seconds per client address without a key or session, 120 per 10 seconds per user or key
